policy_name: Guidelines for Use of Generative AI
issuing_authority: Gray Media (AI Policy Team, Legal Team and Technology Team)
country_region: United States (Gray Media, broadcast and digital media company)
regulatory_regime: Corporate internal AI use policy (newsroom and business)
geo_constraints: Gray employees, General Managers and department heads; AI vendors used by Gray

locale_context.regulation: Internal policy · corporate generative AI use rules
locale_context.culture: US local-broadcast newsroom ethics: public trust and human-created journalism come first, with AI allowed as a vetted, overseeable tool and transparency to audiences.

versions.title: October 2025
versions.summary: Only one version recorded for this policy.

covered_systems: AI vendor services (transcription, commercial scriptwriting, graphics/image development, AI-generated content)
covered_activities: editorial, creative and business use of generative AI
exceptions: exceptions require explicit approval/authorisation by the AI Policy Team (confidential data sharing; tools without human override)
conditions: employees must complete training before being approved to use AI
objective: Allow responsible, helpful use of generative AI while maintaining public trust in Gray's journalism: human-created news, vetted vendors, data protection and human oversight.

record_provenance.notes: Text taken from the copy in asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper (policy_examples/gray.pdf). (asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper commit b8ac8876beec6593ef5685d7d7e64cc94f9cc55b.) One-page document dated 'October 2025' (no day, no version number); the issuer is identified as Gray from the text and the aipolicy@graymedia.com contact, and its full corporate name is not printed. No official URL is printed, so the asago copy is the source_uri; whether this is the latest version is not verified. Titled 'Guidelines' but phrased as mandatory rules for employees and vendors, so recorded as an enforceable internal policy. Binding=false: not law, but mandatory for Gray employees.

clauses.original_text: All Gray-originated news content is to be created by humans. Where generative AI can enhance our abilities to serve the public, Gray will prioritize transparency to our audiences.
clauses.action: create by humans; be transparent to audiences
clauses.requirement: news content is human-created; AI use is transparent to audiences
clauses.affected_asset: accuracy and integrity of news; audience trust
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from the asago copy of the one-page PDF; line breaks collapsed. One of the two core tenets informing the policy.

clauses.original_text: ALL AI vendors must be vetted and approved by a member of the Gray Legal Team and the Gray Technology Team. This includes services such as transcription, commercial scriptwriting, graphics/image development, and any use of AI-generated content.
clauses.requirement: Legal and Technology approval of every AI vendor before use
clauses.purpose: manage legal, IP and security risks
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from the asago copy of the one-page PDF; line breaks collapsed. Untitled paragraph; section label is the compiler's. Staff are expected to review the approved vendors and use-case documents regularly.

clauses.original_text: Unless explicitly approved by the AI Policy Team, users of AI tools are prohibited from sharing confidential or sensitive information with generative AI tools, including but not limited to employee identifying information, passwords, or other proprietary information.
clauses.requirement: no confidential/sensitive data in generative AI tools without AI Policy Team approval
clauses.exception: explicit approval by the AI Policy Team
clauses.affected_asset: employee personal data; passwords; proprietary information
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI tools and AI vendors used at Gray
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from the asago copy of the one-page PDF; line breaks collapsed. Untitled paragraph; section label is the compiler's.

clauses.original_text: Employees who are appropriately trained to use an approved AI tool must protect their login credentials. When available, multi-factor authentication should be used for AI tools.
clauses.requirement: protect AI tool credentials and use MFA when available
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from the asago copy of the one-page PDF; line breaks collapsed. MFA is a SHOULD ('when available').

clauses.original_text: AI tools will be evaluated regularly for fairness and bias.
clauses.requirement: regular fairness and bias evaluation of AI tools
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI tools and AI vendors used at Gray
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from the asago copy of the one-page PDF; line breaks collapsed. Evaluator is not named.

clauses.original_text: Unless explicitly authorized by the AI Policy Team, only AI tools that give employees the ability to override AI will be approved for use. Human oversight must always be present with the use of any AI technology.
clauses.action: approve only overridable tools; maintain human oversight
clauses.object: AI tools and any AI technology
clauses.requirement: only AI tools with human override; human oversight always present
clauses.exception: explicit authorisation by the AI Policy Team (for tools without override)
clauses.purpose: keep humans in control of AI
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI tools and AI vendors used at Gray
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from the asago copy of the one-page PDF; line breaks collapsed. Untitled paragraph; section label is the compiler's.
